name: Upwork
summary: Freelance marketplace where clients post jobs, hire and pay freelancers, with fees charged on payments instead of a flat plan price.
best_for: small businesses and teams that need to find and pay freelancers on a project basis and want one place for contracts and payments
skip_if: you want a fixed monthly price, you hire the same person long term and would rather pay them directly, or you need a plan comparison we could not verify
honest_knock: There is no flat plan price to compare: the cost is a percentage on every payment, charged to the client and separately to the freelancer. The Client Marketplace Fee is not refundable even if the payment is refunded, and the client pricing pages were not readable for us, so the paid-plan features are not verified.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-23 on support.upwork.com help articles; the client pricing pages returned an access error, so there is no complete plan table) Upwork is a marketplace where clients hire freelancers, and it earns through fees on payments rather than a single subscription price. Its help article on the Client Marketplace Fee describes the Basic client plan as free and says payments made to freelancers carry a Client Marketplace Fee of up to 7.99%, which is not refundable even when the underlying payment is refunded. A Business Plus client pays a 10% fee on freelancer payments, and eligible US Business Plus clients may qualify for a reduced 8% fee when paying from a checking account. Freelancers pay a separate service fee of 0% to 15% per contract, fixed once the contract begins, and Upwork returns the freelancer service fee on any amount that is refunded. Freelancers bid with Connects, which cost $0.15 (USD) each. Enterprise pricing and the Connects allowances per membership are not published in the pages we read. Client and freelancer fees are separate and should not be added into one price.
